bedroom.guidance: Make the bed the clear sleeping focal point and keep balanced bedside access where the room permits.
Use an intentionally asymmetric sleeping zone while preserving a direct door-to-bed circulation route.
Create distinct sleeping and compact work zones with neither zone borrowing the other's required access space.
Create a sleeping zone and a genuinely usable reading corner with a seat facing a meaningful direction or point.
Make storage access a first-class zone while retaining a calm sleeping area and a clear route from the door.

living_room.guidance: Organize the seating around a media or focal wall and preserve a usable central circulation route.
Organize seating for conversation rather than a single media-facing line, with a coherent shared table relationship.
Use a main lounge zone plus a separate but connected reading seat zone.
Prioritize a broad, legible door-to-primary-zone route and keep furniture grouped away from that route.
Use an intentionally asymmetric lounge composition that still reads as balanced and usable.

dining_room.guidance: Create a conventional four-seat dining arrangement with every chair usable and the table as the activity center.
Create a usable six-seat dining arrangement; do not add six chairs unless their pullout and circulation space can remain valid.
Use a dining bench with chairs only when the resulting mixed seating arrangement remains practical and accessible.
Pair the dining zone with a wall-based service or storage zone while retaining a clear route around the table.
Place the dining group off the room center only when this creates a clearer usable route than a centered arrangement.

home_office.guidance: Use a wall-backed desk workstation with a correctly aligned chair and clear work access.
Place the workstation near, but never in, the window clearance zone and preserve useful light-oriented organization.
Use a freestanding desk only when the room still has clear circulation and the chair pullout remains usable.
Create distinct work and reading zones without treating a side table or lamp as a seat's facing target.
Make desk work and storage both usable, with independent front access to storage.
